ax: What is the tool for and how is it driven: worn for protection, carried for storage, used to measure, joined with heat, held in the hand and powered, worked by hand, fixed in a workshop, or a lift or site machine?
key: 1. Is it worn to protect the body (helmet, glasses, ear defenders, respirator, gloves, harness)? → Protective equipment (PPE)
2. Does it hold, carry or store tools (box, chest, bag, belt)? → Tool storage
3. Does it read a size, angle, level, distance or electrical or physical value? → Measuring & detecting
4. Does it join or cut metal with heat (welder, torch, soldering iron) or is it the wire, solder or flux they use? → Welding & soldering
5. Is it a ladder, or something that lifts, jacks, hauls or wheels a load? → Ladders, lifting & moving
6. Is it an engine- or mains-driven machine for a site or yard (generator, compressor, pump, mixer, compactor)? → Site equipment & power
7. Is it a bench or floor machine that the work is brought to (table saw, lathe, drill press, CNC)? → Workshop machinery
8. Is it a hand-held tool run by a battery, mains motor or compressed air, or a bit, blade or disc that fits one? → Power tools
9. Is it a knife, multi-tool, axe or other carried or chopping edge? → Knives, multi-tools & axes
10. Is it a hand tool used on wood alone (plane, saw, chisel, gouge, clamp, bench)? → Woodworking hand tools
11. Is it any other hand tool (spanner, pliers, hammer, trowel, pipe tool, sharpening stone)? → General hand tools

Precedence: a mains-powered tool that is hand-held is a power tool (step 8) even when a bench version exists (step 7); a knife or saw for wood goes to its own department only when it is carried (step 9) or worked by hand on wood (step 10); a pocket sharpener lives with the sharpening stones in General hand tools.
